answer: According to Section 351(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, whoever commits the offense of criminal intimidation by an anonymous communication, or takes precautions to conceal their identity, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, in addition to any other punishment provided for the offense under subsection (1).
summary_answer: The punishment for criminal intimidation can extend to two years of imprisonment if the offense is committed anonymously.
detailed_answer: According to Section 351(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, whoever commits the offense of criminal intimidation by an anonymous communication, or takes precautions to conceal their identity, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, in addition to any other punishment provided for the offense under subsection (1).
final_answer: The punishment for criminal intimidation can extend to two years of imprisonment, especially if committed anonymously.
